rounds.proof_sketch: With block_size(256,1), threadIdx.y=0 for all threads. All 256 threads write to same 3 shared memory locations (channels=3) before reading. Both versions have identical race condition - __syncthreads() ensures write completion but doesn't determine which of 256 competing writes wins. Race outcome is hardware-scheduling-dependent, not value-dependent.
rounds.survival_reason: The kernel has a fundamental race condition where all 256 threads in a block write to the same 3 shared memory locations (channel_vals[0..2]). With blockDim.y=1, there is no cooperative loading - each thread independently writes all channels. The __syncthreads() barrier only ensures synchronization between writes and reads but doesn't resolve which write wins the race. Without the barrier, the race still exists but reads may interleave with writes. Since CUDA thread scheduling is hardware-determined and not controllable via input values, no value-level test can deterministically expose a difference between the two versions.
rounds.kill_strategy: Cannot kill through value-level testing. The difference depends on CUDA thread scheduling which is not controllable through input tensor values. Both versions have identical shared memory race conditions.
rounds.recommendations: This kernel has a correctness bug: with block_size(256,1), all threads share 3 floats of shared memory but write different values to them. The shared memory allocation should be channels * blockDim.x * sizeof(float), or the kernel should use registers/local memory for per-thread channel storage. The __syncthreads() removal mutation is unkillable because the underlying race condition dominates any synchronization difference.
